title: CUET Political Science Test 15
subject: Political Science (Code: 323)
syllabus_source: CUET SYLLABUS/Political Science - 323.pdf (NTA syllabus for CUET (UG) 2026, latest published)
past_paper_reference: Pattern benchmark only: NTA CUET (UG) Political Science papers 2024 and 2026, analysed for format only (no questions copied)
textbooks: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence
instructions: Each correct answer earns 5 marks; each incorrect answer deducts 1 mark; unattempted questions earn 0.
One set of 5 questions is based on a passage; the set stays together.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: South Asia in the Post-Cold War Era
questions.sub_topic: Why the Maoists grew strong in Nepal
questions.question: Why did the Maoists gain influence in Nepal?
options: A) They waged an armed revolt against the monarchy.
B) The king had invited them to form the army.
C) India had installed them in power in 1990.
D) They had won every election since 1950.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) They waged an armed revolt against the monarchy.
Why: The Maoists drew support from rural areas by waging an armed insurgency against the monarchy and the ruling elite.
Why not the others:
(B) The king fought them.
(C) India did not install them.
(D) They had not won every election.
Key point: The Maoist insurgency helped bring down the monarchy.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Regional Aspirations and Conflicts
questions.sub_topic: A lesson about regional aspirations
questions.question: What lesson does NCERT draw about regional aspirations in India?
options: A) They should be suppressed by force wherever they arise.
B) They are part of democracy and can be met by talks.
C) They always lead to the break-up of the country.
D) They exist only in the border States of the North-East.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) They are part of democracy and can be met by talks.
Why: NCERT argues that regional demands are a normal part of democracy and are best handled by dialogue and accommodation.
Why not the others:
(A) Force is not the lesson drawn.
(C) Most have been accommodated within India.
(D) They arise in many parts of India.
Key point: Accommodation, not suppression, strengthens national unity.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.sub_topic: When the World Bank was created
questions.question: The World Bank was created in ________.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 1944
Why: The World Bank was created at the Bretton Woods conference in 1944.
Why not the others:
(B), (C) and (D) are later dates; 1995 is when the WTO was set up.
Key point: The World Bank and IMF date from the end of the Second World War.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Security in the Contemporary World
questions.sub_topic: Not one of the kinds of human rights NCERT names
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the categories of human rights discussed under human security?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Rights of corporations
Why: NCERT names political rights, economic and social rights, and the rights of colonised and indigenous peoples. Corporations are not a category.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are the categories NCERT lists.
Key point: Human rights violations are a concern of human security.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.sub_topic: Organ headed by the Secretary-General
questions.question: The UN Secretary-General is the head of the ________.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Secretariat
Why: The Secretary-General heads the Secretariat, the UN's administrative organ.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are separate organs with their own presidents or members.
Key point: The Secretary-General is the UN's chief administrative officer.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Security in the Contemporary World
questions.sub_topic: Responses to threats in traditional security
questions.question:
Match List-I (Response) with List-II (Meaning).

List-I
(A) Deterrence
(B) Defence
(C) Alliance building
(D) Surrender

List-II
(I) Forming coalitions with other states against a threat
(II) Giving in to the enemy
(III) Preventing war by threatening unacceptable costs
(IV) Limiting or ending a war once it has begun
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
Why: Deterrence prevents war (III). Defence limits or ends it (IV). Alliance building means forming coalitions (I). Surrender means giving in (II).
Why not the others: Option (A) swaps deterrence and defence. Option (B) swaps defence and alliance building. Option (D) swaps alliance building and surrender.
Key point: States respond to external threats in several ways.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Crises of the Constitutional Order
questions.sub_topic: Government's justification for the Emergency
questions.question: How did the government justify the declaration of the Emergency in 1975?
options: A) It said a foreign army had invaded India.
B) It said the economy had grown too fast.
C) It said agitations threatened order.
D) It said the courts had asked for an Emergency.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) It said agitations threatened order.
Why: The government argued that the opposition's agitations were creating disorder and threatening the country's stability.
Why not the others:
(A) There was no invasion.
(B) The economy was in difficulty, not growing too fast.
(D) The courts made no such request.
Key point: The Emergency was declared on grounds of internal disturbance.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Nation-Building and Its Problems
questions.sub_topic: Telugu State created in 1953
questions.question: The demand of Telugu speakers was met in 1953 with the creation of ________ State.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Andhra
Why: Andhra State was formed in 1953 for Telugu speakers.
Why not the others:
(B) Gujarat was formed in 1960.
(C) Punjab was reorganised in 1966.
(D) Mysore State (later Karnataka) took shape in 1956.
Key point: Andhra opened the way for the 1956 reorganisation.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.sub_topic: What lies behind four environmental problems
questions.question:
Match List-I (Problem) with List-II (Main cause).

List-I
(A) Global warming
(B) Ozone depletion
(C) Desertification
(D) Loss of biodiversity

List-II
(I) Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)
(II) Destruction of natural habitats
(III) Degradation of dry land
(IV) Greenhouse gas emissions
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(II)
Why: Global warming comes from greenhouse gases (IV). Ozone depletion comes from CFCs (I). Desertification is the degradation of dry land (III). Biodiversity is lost when habitats are destroyed (II).
Why not the others: Option (A) swaps global warming and ozone depletion. Option (B) swaps ozone depletion and desertification. Option (C) swaps desertification and biodiversity.
Key point: Environmental problems have distinct causes needing distinct responses.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.sub_topic: Congress leadership, 1964–1971, in order
questions.question:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
(A) Lal Bahadur Shastri dies at Tashkent
(B) The Congress splits
(C) Jawaharlal Nehru dies
(D) Indira Gandhi wins a big majority in the Lok Sabha election
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (C), (A), (B), (D)
Why: (C) Nehru died in 1964. (A) Shastri died in 1966. (B) The Congress split in 1969. (D) Indira Gandhi won the 1971 election.
Why not the others: Option (B) puts Shastri's death before Nehru's. Option (C) puts the split before Shastri's death. Option (D) puts the 1971 victory before the split.
Key point: 1964 → 1966 → 1969 → 1971.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Recent Issues and Challenges
questions.sub_topic: Ayodhya, the BJP and the BSP, 1980–1995, in order
questions.question:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
(A) L.K. Advani leads a rath yatra from Somnath towards Ayodhya
(B) The BJP is formed
(C) The locks of the disputed structure at Ayodhya are opened
(D) The BSP forms a government in Uttar Pradesh for the first time
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (B), (C), (A), (D)
Why: (B) The BJP was formed in 1980. (C) The locks were opened in 1986. (A) The rath yatra came in 1990. (D) The BSP formed its first government in UP in 1995.
Why not the others: Option (A) puts the rath yatra before the opening of the locks. Option (B) puts the locks before the BJP's formation. Option (C) puts the BSP government before the rath yatra.
Key point: 1980 → 1986 → 1990 → 1995.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.sub_topic: Environmental agreements, 1959–1997, in order
questions.question:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
(A) The Kyoto Protocol is agreed
(B) The Antarctic Treaty is signed
(C) The Montreal Protocol is signed
(D) The Earth Summit meets at Rio
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (B), (C), (D), (A)
Why: (B) The Antarctic Treaty came in 1959. (C) The Montreal Protocol came in 1987. (D) The Earth Summit met in 1992. (A) The Kyoto Protocol was agreed in 1997.
Why not the others: Option (B) puts Montreal before the Antarctic Treaty. Option (C) puts Rio before Montreal. Option (D) puts Kyoto before Rio.
Key point: 1959 → 1987 → 1992 → 1997.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Regional Aspirations and Conflicts
questions.sub_topic: Not one of the 'Seven Sisters'
questions.question: Which of the following States is NOT one of the 'Seven Sisters' of the North-East?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Sikkim
Why: The Seven Sisters are Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura. Sikkim is not among them.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are among the Seven Sisters.
Key point: Sikkim joined India separately in 1975.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Globalisation and Its Critics
questions.sub_topic: An example of outsourcing to India
questions.question: Which of the following is a common example of work outsourced to India under globalisation?
options: B) Call centres for foreign companies
C) Traditional handloom weaving for local use
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Call centres for foreign companies
Why: Many foreign companies run call centres and back-office work in India.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are not outsourced work.
Key point: Outsourcing has created new jobs in India's service sector.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Nation-Building and Its Problems
questions.sub_topic: What the 'two-nation theory' claimed
questions.question: The 'two-nation theory' advanced by the Muslim League held that:
options: A) India and Pakistan should share a single government
B) the British and the Indians formed two separate nations
C) India should be divided into North and South India
D) Hindus and Muslims formed two separate nations
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Hindus and Muslims formed two separate nations
Why: The theory claimed that India consisted of two nations, Hindus and Muslims, and that Muslims needed a separate homeland.
Why not the others:
(A) The theory led to separate states.
(B) It was about religious communities, not the British.
(C) It had nothing to do with north and south.
Key point: The two-nation theory was rejected by the Congress but led to Partition.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Era of One-Party Dominance
questions.sub_topic: Role of the opposition in the era of Congress dominance
questions.question: Why did the opposition parties matter in the 1950s even though they won few seats?
options: A) Because their criticism kept a check on the ruling party
B) Because they ran the Central government by turns
C) Because they had a veto over all bills in Parliament
D) Because they controlled the Election Commission
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Because their criticism kept a check on the ruling party
Why: Opposition parties offered sustained and principled criticism of Congress policies and kept its power in check.
Why not the others:
(B) The Congress ran the Centre.
(C) No party had such a veto.
(D) The Election Commission is independent.
Key point: A small opposition still kept democracy alive and alert.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Nation-Building and Its Problems
questions.sub_topic: Integrating the princely states — which hold
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) There were more than 560 princely states at independence.
(B) Hyderabad was integrated into India in 1948 after military action.
(C) Manipur held elections to a legislative assembly on the basis of universal adult franchise in 1948.
(D) The Instrument of Accession of Jammu and Kashmir was signed by Sheikh Abdullah.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) are correct. (D) is wrong: the Instrument of Accession was signed by Maharaja Hari Singh.
Why not the others: Option (A) leaves out the true statement (C). Options (B) and (D) include the false statement (D).
Key point: Integration involved persuasion, pressure and, in Hyderabad, force.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Crises of the Constitutional Order
questions.sub_topic: An excess of the Emergency period
questions.question: Among the excesses of the Emergency period was a drive of forced ________.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) sterilisation
Why: The Shah Commission found that people had been forced to undergo sterilisation.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) were not part of the Emergency's excesses.
Key point: Forced sterilisation and slum demolitions caused public anger.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.sub_topic: Why the Soviet Union fell behind the West
questions.question: Why did the Soviet Union fall behind the West by the 1980s?
options: A) Because it had no natural resources at all
B) Because it spent nothing on its armed forces
C) Because it lagged in technology and infrastructure
D) Because its population was too small to work
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Because it lagged in technology and infrastructure
Why: The Soviet economy stagnated and fell behind the West in technology and infrastructure.
Why not the others:
(A) The USSR was rich in resources.
(B) It spent heavily on arms.
(D) It had a large population.
Key point: Stagnation and technological lag fed the crisis of the system.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Era of One-Party Dominance
questions.sub_topic: What made the 1957 Kerala government unusual
questions.question: The Communist government formed in Kerala in 1957 was one of the first in the world to come to power through ________.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) democratic elections
Why: The CPI-led government in Kerala came to power by winning an election, which was rare for Communist parties then.
Why not the others:
(A) There was no revolution.
(C) No foreign power was involved.
(D) India had no royal decrees.
Key point: Kerala showed Communists could win power through the ballot.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.sub_topic: Interim Prime Minister in 1964 and 1966
questions.question: After the deaths of Nehru and Shastri, ________ served for a short time as interim Prime Minister on both occasions.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Gulzarilal Nanda
Why: Gulzarilal Nanda was interim Prime Minister in 1964 and again in 1966.
Why not the others:
(A) Morarji Desai became PM only in 1977.
(B) Kamaraj was Congress President.
(C) Yashwantrao Chavan never became PM.
Key point: Nanda twice bridged the gap in leadership.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Alternative Centres of Economic and Political Power
questions.sub_topic: The EU, ASEAN and India–China ties — the false claim
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) The EU has its own flag, anthem and currency.
(B) Many EU members have adopted the euro as their currency.
(C) Trade between India and China has grown greatly in recent decades.
(D) All EU members are bound by a single common foreign and defence policy.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (D) only
Why: Only (D) is false: EU members keep their own foreign and defence policies and often differ.
Why not the others: (A) The EU has a flag, anthem and currency. (B) Many members use the euro. (C) India–China trade has grown. Options (A), (B) and (D) name a true statement as false.
Key point: The EU's unity is limited in foreign and defence policy.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.sub_topic: Outcome that did not follow the Soviet break-up
questions.question: Which one of these did NOT result from the break-up of the USSR?
options: A) The end of the Cold War
B) Faster growth of the Soviet economy
C) The emergence of many new countries
D) A shift in the world balance of power
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Faster growth of the Soviet economy
Why: The Soviet economy ceased to exist with the USSR; it did not grow faster.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) were consequences of the collapse.
Key point: The collapse transformed world politics.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.sub_topic: India's per capita carbon emissions
questions.question: In 2000, India's per capita carbon dioxide emission was only about ________ tonnes a year.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 0.9
Why: India's per capita emission was about 0.9 tonnes in 2000, far below the world average.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are far above India's figure.
Key point: Low per capita emissions underpin India's case in climate talks.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.sub_topic: Seat Russia took over from the USSR
questions.question: After 1991, Russia took over the Soviet Union's permanent seat in the ________.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) UN Security Council
Why: Russia inherited the USSR's permanent seat in the UN Security Council.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) never had a Soviet seat to inherit.
Key point: Russia is the successor state of the USSR.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.sub_topic: Facts about the UN — which hold
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) The UN has 193 member states.
(B) The permanent members of the Security Council are the US, Russia, the UK, France and China.
(C) The headquarters of the UN is in New York.
(D) The UN Charter was signed at Geneva.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) are correct. (D) is wrong: the Charter was signed at San Francisco.
Why not the others: Option (A) leaves out the true statement (B). Options (C) and (D) include the false statement (D).
Key point: The UN was founded at San Francisco in 1945.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.sub_topic: Leaders of the Soviet Union and Russia
questions.question:
Match List-I (Leader) with List-II (Description).

List-I
(A) Lenin
(B) Stalin
(C) Gorbachev
(D) Yeltsin

List-II
(I) Led the resistance to the hardliners' coup of 1991
(II) Founder of the Bolshevik party and leader of the 1917 revolution
(III) Ruled from 1924 to 1953 and drove rapid industrialisation
(IV) The last leader of the Soviet Union
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I)
Why: Lenin founded the Bolshevik party and led the revolution (II). Stalin ruled from 1924 to 1953 (III). Gorbachev was the last Soviet leader (IV). Yeltsin led the resistance to the 1991 coup (I).
Why not the others: Option (B) swaps Lenin and Stalin. Option (C) swaps Stalin and Gorbachev. Option (D) swaps Gorbachev and Yeltsin.
Key point: Soviet history runs from Lenin's revolution to Gorbachev's fall.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Crises of the Constitutional Order
questions.sub_topic: Figures of the 1970s opposition
questions.question:
Match List-I (Leader) with List-II (Description).

List-I
(A) Morarji Desai
(B) Charan Singh
(C) Jayaprakash Narayan
(D) George Fernandes

List-II
(I) Became Prime Minister in 1979
(II) Led the nationwide railway strike of 1974
(III) First non-Congress Prime Minister of India
(IV) Called for 'Total Revolution'
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)
Why: Morarji Desai was the first non-Congress PM (III). Charan Singh became PM in 1979 (I). JP called for Total Revolution (IV). George Fernandes led the 1974 railway strike (II).
Why not the others: Option (A) swaps Desai and Charan Singh. Option (C) swaps Charan Singh and JP. Option (D) swaps JP and Fernandes.
Key point: Varied leaders came together against the Congress in the 1970s.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Democratic Upsurge and Coalition Politics
questions.sub_topic: Coalition-era governments — which hold
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) The Narasimha Rao government launched the new economic policies in 1991.
(B) The UPA came to power in 2004.
(C) The NDA government formed in 1999 completed its full term.
(D) The Congress won an absolute majority in the 1996 election.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) are correct. (D) is wrong: no party won a majority in 1996.
Why not the others: Option (B) leaves out the true statement (C). Options (C) and (D) include the false statement (D).
Key point: Coalition governments became the norm after 1989.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Regional Aspirations and Conflicts
questions.sub_topic: Leaders and organisations of regional movements
questions.question:
Match List-I (Leader or body) with List-II (Description).

List-I
(A) Sheikh Abdullah
(B) Laldenga
(C) AASU
(D) Sant Harchand Singh Longowal

List-II
(I) Akali leader who signed the Punjab accord
(II) Student body that led the Assam movement
(III) Leader of the Mizo National Front
(IV) Leader of the National Conference in Kashmir
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: Sheikh Abdullah led the National Conference (IV). Laldenga led the MNF (III). AASU led the Assam movement (II). Longowal signed the Punjab accord (I).
Why not the others: Option (A) swaps Abdullah and Laldenga. Option (B) swaps Laldenga and AASU. Option (D) swaps AASU and Longowal.
Key point: Regional movements were led by parties, students and religious leaders.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: South Asia in the Post-Cold War Era
questions.sub_topic: From the Maldives republic to a Nepali republic, in sequence
questions.question:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
(A) Bangladesh becomes independent
(B) Nepal abolishes its monarchy
(C) SAARC is established
(D) The Maldives becomes a republic
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (D), (A), (C), (B)
Why: (D) The Maldives became a republic in 1968. (A) Bangladesh became independent in 1971. (C) SAARC was set up in 1985. (B) Nepal abolished the monarchy in 2008.
Why not the others: Option (A) puts Bangladesh before the Maldives. Option (B) puts SAARC before Bangladesh. Option (D) puts Nepal before SAARC.
Key point: 1968 → 1971 → 1985 → 2008.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Globalisation and Its Critics
questions.sub_topic: Globalisation and India — spot the error
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Globalisation began only in the 1990s and has no earlier history.
(B) Globalisation has led to a growing role for multinational companies.
(C) The reforms of 1991 opened up the Indian economy.
(D) Globalisation affects different countries and groups differently.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A) only
Why: Only (A) is false: flows of people, goods and ideas across the world have a long history.
Why not the others: (B) MNCs have grown in importance. (C) The 1991 reforms opened the economy. (D) Its effects are uneven. Options (A), (B) and (C) name a true statement as false.
Key point: Globalisation is not new, though its pace has quickened.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Alternative Centres of Economic and Political Power
questions.sub_topic: US programme that rebuilt Western Europe
questions.question: After the Second World War, the US helped rebuild the economies of Western Europe through the ________ Plan.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Marshall
Why: The Marshall Plan gave aid for Europe's recovery.
Why not the others:
(A) The Colombo Plan concerned Asia.
(B) The Bombay Plan was drafted by Indian industrialists.
(C) The Molotov Plan was a Soviet scheme for Eastern Europe.
Key point: US aid encouraged European cooperation.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: India's External Relations
questions.sub_topic: Why India turned to the USSR in 1971
questions.question: Why did India sign a treaty of friendship with the USSR in 1971?
options: A) Because it wanted to join the Warsaw Pact
B) Because the USSR had promised to fund all Five Year Plans
C) Because it faced a growing US–China–Pakistan alignment
D) Because the UN had asked it to seek a Soviet ally
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Because it faced a growing US–China–Pakistan alignment
Why: With the US and China drawing close to Pakistan, India sought Soviet support through the 1971 treaty.
Why not the others:
(A) India did not join the Warsaw Pact.
(B) No such promise was made.
(D) The UN made no such request.
Key point: The 1971 treaty was a response to a changing balance in the region.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Era of One-Party Dominance
questions.sub_topic: Leaders of the first decade after independence
questions.question:
Match List-I (Leader) with List-II (Description).

List-I
(A) Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
(B) Deen Dayal Upadhyaya
(C) E.M.S. Namboodiripad
(D) Sukumar Sen

List-II
(I) Chief Minister of the Communist government of Kerala in 1957
(II) India's first Education Minister
(III) Chief Election Commissioner in the first general election
(IV) Jana Sangh leader who put forward 'integral humanism'
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(III)
Why: Azad was India's first Education Minister (II). Upadhyaya put forward 'integral humanism' (IV). Namboodiripad led the Kerala government of 1957 (I). Sukumar Sen ran the first general election (III).
Why not the others: Option (A) swaps Azad and Upadhyaya. Option (B) swaps Upadhyaya and Namboodiripad. Option (C) swaps Namboodiripad and Sukumar Sen.
Key point: Leaders of many shades shaped the early republic.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: South Asia in the Post-Cold War Era
questions.sub_topic: Communities in Sri Lanka's ethnic conflict
questions.question: The ethnic conflict in Sri Lanka has been between the Sinhalas and the ________.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Tamils
Why: The conflict was between the Sinhala majority and the Tamil minority.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are not part of Sri Lanka's conflict.
Key point: Tamil grievances fuelled a long civil war.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Globalisation and Its Critics
questions.sub_topic: Why some on the right criticise globalisation
questions.question: Why do some critics on the political right oppose globalisation?
options: A) Because it makes the state too strong
B) Because it may weaken the state and harm traditional culture
C) Because it ends the role of all multinational companies
D) Because it stops the movement of capital
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Because it may weaken the state and harm traditional culture
Why: Critics on the right fear the weakening of the state and the loss of traditional culture.
Why not the others:
(A) They fear a weaker state, not a stronger one.
(C) MNCs grow under globalisation.
(D) Capital moves more freely.
Key point: Critics on both left and right oppose globalisation for different reasons.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Security in the Contemporary World
questions.sub_topic: Arms control treaty of 1972
questions.question: The treaty signed by the US and the USSR in 1972 to limit missile defence systems was the ________ Treaty.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Anti-Ballistic Missile
Why: The ABM Treaty of 1972 limited missile defence systems.
Why not the others:
(B) The NPT was signed in 1968.
(C) The CTBT came in 1996.
(D) The CWC came in 1992.
Key point: Arms control regulates rather than abolishes weapons.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Alternative Centres of Economic and Political Power
questions.sub_topic: European state outside the EU
questions.question: Which European country listed below has chosen to stay outside the European Union?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Norway
Why: Norway has chosen to stay outside the EU.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are EU members.
Key point: Not every European country belongs to the EU.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Democratic Upsurge and Coalition Politics
questions.sub_topic: Second Prime Minister of the United Front
questions.question: After H.D. Deve Gowda, the United Front government was led by ________.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) I.K. Gujral
Why: I.K. Gujral succeeded Deve Gowda as United Front Prime Minister in 1997.
Why not the others:
(A) Chandra Shekhar was PM in 1990–91.
(B) Rao was PM from 1991 to 1996.
(D) V.P. Singh was PM in 1989–90.
Key point: The United Front had two Prime Ministers in two years.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: Alternative Centres of Economic and Political Power
questions.sub_topic: Why India and China are seen as rising powers
questions.question: Why are India and China often expected to become major world powers?
options: A) Their size and fast-growing economies
B) Both hold permanent UNSC seats
C) Both belong to the European Union
D) Both have given up their armies
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Their size and fast-growing economies
Why: Their size, resources and fast-growing economies make both likely major powers.
Why not the others:
(B) Only China is a permanent member.
(C) Neither is in the EU.
(D) Both maintain large forces.
Key point: Economic growth is the basis of their rise.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.sub_topic: Voting power in the IMF
questions.question: What is the main complaint developing countries make about how the IMF takes decisions?
options: A) It needs every member's approval for each loan
B) Only the poorest countries are allowed to vote
C) Rich countries hold most of the voting power
D) The General Assembly controls all its votes
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Rich countries hold most of the voting power
Why: Votes in the IMF depend on contributions, so a handful of rich countries hold a large share of the voting power.
Why not the others:
(A) No such rule exists.
(B) Rich countries dominate it.
(D) It is a separate institution.
Key point: Unequal voting is a central criticism of the IMF.

questions.topic: Contemporary World Politics: South Asia in the Post-Cold War Era
questions.sub_topic: Regional grouping that Myanmar belongs to
questions.question: India's eastern neighbour Myanmar is not in SAARC. It is a member of ________.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) ASEAN
Why: Myanmar joined ASEAN in 1997.
Why not the others:
(A) The EU is European.
(B) NAFTA covers North America.
(C) OPEC is a group of oil exporters.
Key point: Myanmar links South Asia and Southeast Asia.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Recent Issues and Challenges
questions.sub_topic: Meaning of secularism in the Indian context
questions.question: In the Indian context, secularism means that:
options: A) the state does not favour any religion and respects all
B) religion is banned from all public life in the country
C) the state follows and promotes the religion of the majority
D) only one religion may be taught in all the schools
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) the state does not favour any religion and respects all
Why: Indian secularism means the state treats all religions with equal respect and does not favour any.
Why not the others:
(B) Religion is not banned.
(C) That would be a religious state.
(D) That contradicts secularism.
Key point: Secularism is the opposite of communalism.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: India's External Relations
questions.sub_topic: Nuclear tests, Kargil and Panchsheel — spot the error
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) India carried out a series of nuclear tests in May 1998.
(B) India described its 1974 test as a peaceful nuclear explosion.
(C) The Kargil conflict took place in 1999.
(D) The Panchsheel principles allowed each side to intervene in the other's internal affairs.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (D) only
Why: Only (D) is false: Panchsheel stressed non-interference in each other's internal affairs.
Why not the others: (A) The tests took place in May 1998. (B) The 1974 test was called peaceful. (C) Kargil was in 1999. Options (A), (C) and (D) name a true statement as false.
Key point: Non-interference was one of the five principles.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Politics of Planned Development
questions.sub_topic: Top priority of the First Plan
questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

Once the Planning Commission had been set up, the central question was what the plans should give priority to. The First Five Year Plan gave the highest priority to agriculture. Large sums were invested in dams and irrigation, and the Bhakra Nangal project was among the most ambitious of these. The planners also saw land reform as the key to rural development. The Second Plan, drawn up under the guidance of P.C. Mahalanobis, shifted the emphasis to heavy industry, in the belief that rapid industrialisation would pull the whole economy forward. This choice did not go unchallenged. Some critics argued that the plans neglected agriculture and had no clear strategy for rural India. Others complained that the public sector grew too powerful and created vested interests of its own, and that the system of licences and permits held back private enterprise. Yet even critics accept that these early plans laid the foundations of India's later growth. The large irrigation and power projects, the steel plants and the heavy industries built in this period served the country for decades.

Question: According to the passage, which sector received the highest priority in the First Five Year Plan?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Agriculture
Why: The passage says the First Plan gave the highest priority to agriculture, with large investments in dams and irrigation.
Why not the others:
(A) Heavy industry became the focus of the Second Plan.
(B) and (D) are not mentioned as priorities.
Key point: The First Plan put farming and irrigation first.

Why: The passage names Bhakra Nangal among the dam and irrigation projects of the First Plan.
Why not the others:

Question: Why, according to the passage, did the Second Plan shift the emphasis to heavy industry?
options: A) Planners thought farming no longer mattered to India.
B) Foreign lenders insisted on industry as a condition of aid.
C) The First Plan had already ended all rural poverty.
D) Planners believed industry would pull the whole economy forward.

Answer: (D) Planners believed industry would pull the whole economy forward.
Why: The passage says the shift rested on the belief that rapid industrialisation would pull the whole economy forward.
Why not the others:

(B) Foreign lenders are not mentioned.
(C) The passage does not claim poverty had ended.

questions.topic: Politics in India since Independence: Politics of Planned Development
questions.sub_topic: Overall judgement of the early plans in the passage

Question: Which statement best sums up the passage's view of the early Five Year Plans?

Why not the others:
